refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: A session is a logical grouping of processes associated with a particular instance of user activity, such as a login session. Each session can optionally have its own vera manager process that is responsible for managing the processes in that session. vera does not create or destroy sessions, this is handled elsewhere, such as by ssh or the desktop environment. vera's role is to manage units for a particular session.

The session manager controls only the units in the &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; hierarchy (see
vera.units 8
for more information). Multiple sessions can exist at the same time. So there can be multiple &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units running at the same time, each under a separate session manager. Regular units are system-wide units, only one instance of a regular unit can be active at a time.
vlad session-start starts a manager for a new session, the session that's running the command. If a unit is specified, this also automatically starts the unit.
Only &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units can be started as part of a session, they cannot be started as regular units.

vlad session-stop stops all active session units (for the command's session), then stops the session's manager. Nothing in the vera package runs session-start automatically. This must be separately arranged. The vera package installs a PAM module, pam_vera, that issues a session-stop command when the user session terminates.

The --session option sends a start, stop, restart, reload, freeze, thaw or status command to the session manager that's running the command. All other options for each command can be used together with the --session option. For example vlad --session --stopped status shows all &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units, including stopped ones, for the current session.
The &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; prefix is optional with session-start and --session. vlad --session start &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX;/gnome and vlad --session start gnome are equivalent.

refsect1.title: DEPENDENCIES
refsect1.para: &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units can depend on other &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units, but cannot depend on regular units. Regular units cannot depend on any &INSTALLED_SESSIONS_PREFIX; units.
